headline: Guru Tegh Bahadur's date is today and his Short is not up yet: publish it by 17:00 IST. The Tipu Sultan Short lapsed this morning with nothing made, so its place goes to a Churchill Short for his birthday on 30 November. Long-form is drawing more viewers but fewer subscribers per view than it used to.

top3.signal: Executed in Delhi in 1675 and remembered on 24 November. His name is trending on X in India and Guru Nanak Jayanti is the second trend, so Sikh history has the day's attention. The searched phrase is “guru tegh bahadur history”. No script is on disk.
top3.recommendation: Publish by 17:00 IST, under a minute, title starting with his name, Aurangzeb in the first sentence. Tell it as an order of state, not a martyr story. Judge it on search views over the year.

top3.signal: Six days out; the recording step falls this week. His English Wikipedia readership is at its usual level, so this rests on the date alone.
top3.recommendation: Record by 27 November and publish on the morning of 30 November, his name first in the title. One document, its date, then what was decided.

top3.signal: 20 days out; the research step falls on 30 November. A named perpetrator, the Pakistan Army and its local allies, and a date.
top3.recommendation: Watch, not yet a decision. If it is made, the killing goes in the first sentence, named and dated: the channel's 1971 refugees video kept its cover-up for late and few saw it.

more.topic: Two films on 4 December: Eetha and Maatrubhumi
more.signal: Both are large releases with trailers out, Eetha a biopic with Shraddha Kapoor and Maatrubhumi a war film with Salman Khan. Neither has a confirmed historical subject in the data.
more.recommendation: Find out by 27 November what each is about. Only a real historical subject gets a Short, published 5 to 13 December, on the story the film leaves out.

skipped.signal: On the calendar for today, and the channel's Tarabai Short is one of its biggest.
skipped.recommendation: Skip. It makes the heroine of that Short the jailer of the boy she put on the throne, and videos that cut down a figure the audience loves are the weakest group on this channel.

skipped.signal: The second trend on X in India, and his English Wikipedia readership is at 2.06x its usual.
skipped.recommendation: Skip a separate Short: a saint's life has no culprit, and saint stories are among the weakest here. Let the Tegh Bahadur Short carry the day.

whats_working: “How the Ramayana Was REWRITTEN to Convert Hindus” carried long-form: long-form views rose 42.4% week over week, and the video has 101,761 views in 6 days. New long-forms have brought 598 subscribers this month against 104 planned, and over 28 days long-form earns 84.0% of the net subscribers videos bring.

The video that brings the most subscribers per view in the 90-day window is still “How One Man Who Never Visited India Wrote Its History”, at 11 net per 1,000 views. Its lesson: “Name the villain, convict him with a document or payment he cannot deny, then end on who is still repeating him today.” The Churchill Short is built on it.

“Why Is Ram Setu Called ADAM'S Bridge?” still draws views every day, nearly three weeks out, from searches such as “ram setu bridge” and “adams bridge”: 12,161 so far. A searched name in the title keeps a Short alive after the feed lets go, which is why the Tegh Bahadur title starts with his name.
whats_wrong: Long-form brings fewer subscribers per view than it used to: 7.4 per 1,000 over the 365-day window, below its usual range. The Ramayana videos pull it down: the Asia one brings 2 per 1,000 and the India one 1.1, and only 41.7% of November's long-form views were engaged. Probable cause: a story with no culprit gets played from the Home feed but not followed. Test: the Bali video names a culprit and a date; compare its subscribers per 1,000 on day three with the Indonesia one's.

Viewers leave the long-forms early: the 7-day average view is down to 27.3%, and all three Ramayana long-forms lose most of their viewers in the first third. Probable cause: Home-feed plays that are not real viewing. Test: not possible on the Indonesia video until its transcript is in the scripts folder, the Bali decision's first step.

Shorts views fell 80.8% week over week to 2026-11-21, and the Ramayana film has stopped carrying Shorts: “Every Ramayana Kept One Rule. The Ramayana Movie BROKE It” (15 November) has 1,761 views against 78,798 for the one of 11 November, though its viewers stayed. Probable cause: the film is in its third week and losing screens. Test: none needed; no more film Shorts, and dated Shorts take the slot.

actions.action: Upload the Malay Ramayana Short (Ravana getting his powers from Allah) on 25 or 26 November, title starting “Ravana”, the Indonesia long-form as its related video, and name the text as the Malay “Hikayat Seri Rama”.
actions.rationale: The script is written from the owner's own draft and was made to send viewers to the Indonesia long-form. Commenters there have already said this version is Malay, so the Short should say so. That it sends viewers on is a guess.

actions.action: Test a new title and the designer's thumbnail on “The Church That Ran Britain's PRISON Camps” in Studio's Test & Compare.
actions.rationale: Over the 365-day window it brings 34.3 subscribers per 1,000 views, the best on the channel, on only 1,078 views: the people who find it subscribe, and too few find it. That the title is the reason is a guess.

actions.action: Check in Studio why “How Jati's evolve organically ?” still has 19 views since 3 November.
actions.rationale: A public Short gets at least a few views a day; this points to a visibility setting or a restriction, not the topic.

actions.action: Set GA4_PROPERTY_ID in .env so the brief can read itiha.info's traffic.
actions.rationale: Search Console alone is thin: every query that shows is the brand name.

growth.verdict: Needs 224 net subscribers a day. The channel does 65.04/day, so the target is a **3.4x** change in rate. Every lever this channel has demonstrated, pulled at once (scenario "1. Current rate, nothing changes"), reaches 65/day — still 3.4x short. At that ceiling rate 100,000 arrives on 2030-05-05, 3.4 years out.

scenarios.name: 1. Current rate, nothing changes
assumptions: Measured: channel_totals_daily, everything the channel publishes, last 28 days.
Same formats, same cadence, same lane mix.
Includes the channel's one breakout: "Chakla: How the British Raj Created a ‘Licensed Vice’ System" is 1282 of the 3,241 subscribers that 22 fresh long-form videos produced.

scenarios.name: 2. Stop Shorts, same effort into long-form (no breakout)
assumptions: Carries the non-upload baseline of 30/day (839 of 1,691 net subscribers over 28 days came from no video). ASSUMPTION: it continues. It currently rests on one viral community post, so treat it as the least safe number here.
Measured: 22 long-form and 105 Shorts published in the last 365 days.
ASSUMPTION (not measured): 6 Shorts cost what 1 long-form costs, so the Shorts become 17.5 more long-form videos a year — 39.5 in total.
Measured: MEDIAN 33 subscribers per fresh long-form video. The mean is 147, inflated by one breakout, so the median is the honest number for planned output.
Gives up the 450 subscribers a year the Shorts brought in; they are simply absent from this total.
Below scenario 1 because scenario 1 contains a breakout and this one does not. That is the point, not an error.

scenarios.name: 3. All long-form, all revision lane (no breakout)
assumptions: Carries the non-upload baseline of 30/day (839 of 1,691 net subscribers over 28 days came from no video). ASSUMPTION: it continues. It currently rests on one viral community post, so treat it as the least safe number here.
Scenario 2's cadence, every topic chosen from the revision lane.
Measured on the same fresh set: 9 revision long-form videos, median 69 subscribers, against 33 for fresh long-form overall.
ASSUMPTION: the lane median holds as output scales. It rests on a small number of videos and is the weakest link here.

scenarios.name: 4. Scenario 3 plus one breakout a quarter
assumptions: Carries the non-upload baseline of 30/day (839 of 1,691 net subscribers over 28 days came from no video). ASSUMPTION: it continues. It currently rests on one viral community post, so treat it as the least safe number here.
Scenario 3, plus four videos a year performing like the best video the channel has ever published.
Measured: "Chakla: How the British Raj Created a ‘Licensed Vice’ System" brought 1,282 subscribers on 73,126 views.
ASSUMPTION: a breakout that size can be produced to order, four times a year. The channel has produced one.
